strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and relevant problem of class imbalance in conditional diffusion models with clear demonstration of the mode collapse phenomenon

Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (ImageNet-LT, TinyImageNet-LT, Places-LT, CIFAR variants), baselines, and architectures with consistent improvements in both quality and diversity metrics
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4-5, multiple figures) clearly demonstrate the contribution of each component with detailed qualitative analysis
Solid technical formulation with clear mathematical derivations and reasonable design choices; framework is generalizable to different architectures (U-Net, Diffusion Transformer)
Good reproducibility practices with detailed implementation details, hyperparameter specifications, and attention to proper evaluation metrics
Practical and easy to implement, demonstrating effectiveness on real-world long-tailed datasets with moderate computational overhead
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: UCL is a straightforward application of standard contrastive learning, and AL reduces to KL divergence minimization—the contribution is primarily combining two existing techniques rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts

Computational cost inadequately addressed: 1.45-1.6× training time increase is mentioned briefly but not thoroughly analyzed; no inference time discussion or guidance on when overhead is justified relative to improvements
Missing statistical rigor: no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance testing despite some improvements being modest; single-seed results limit confidence in claims

Insufficient analysis of failure cases and limitations: no discussion of scenarios where the method underperforms, which classes benefit most/least, or when conditional-unconditional alignment might be suboptimal

Hyperparameter selection and sensitivity not adequately explored: α and γ weights appear fixed across experiments without justification; no sensitivity analysis as these weights vary across different datasets

Theoretical justification gaps: limited formal analysis for why aligning conditional and unconditional generation specifically helps tail classes; connection between UCL and diversity could be more rigorously established
Limited scope and generalization: only evaluated on class-conditional image generation; unclear if insights transfer to other conditional generation tasks or modalities
Experimental design concerns: different guidance strength schedules used for different methods; hyperparameter differences between compared baselines could introduce bias

strengths: Well-motivated problem with practical significance: addresses real-world challenge of class imbalance in diffusion model training with clear improvements (~20% FID_tail improvement on ImageNet-LT 256×256)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets (ImageNet-LT, TinyImageNet-LT, Places-LT, CIFAR variants), architectures (U-Net, Diffusion Transformer), training steps (250k-900k), and metrics (FID, IS, FID_tail, KID, Precision, Recall)
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 4-5, 12-14) systematically validating each component, hyperparameter choices (α, γ), and design decisions (latent representation, time scheduler, batch resampling)
Strong qualitative results clearly demonstrating improved diversity and fidelity for tail classes (Figures 5, 8-10), with effective visualization of mode collapse mitigation
Technically sound mathematical framework with proper derivations (KL decomposition in Eq. 2-7) and good implementation details supporting reproducibility across architectures
Clear presentation of methodology with intuitive figures (Figure 3) explaining the overall framework and synergy between the two proposed loss components
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: UCL is essentially InfoNCE with negative-only sampling (similar to existing Dispersive Loss); conditional-unconditional alignment follows prior GAN work (UTLO, Transition-GAN); primary contribution is combining known techniques for diffusion models rather than developing fundamentally new methods

Insufficient theoretical justification for key design choices: (1) Why negative sampling without positive pairs improves tail diversity lacks deep analysis; (2) Linear time weighting schedule chosen empirically (Table 14) without intuitive explanation; (3) Choice of N-th layer for latent representation (Table 5) lacks principled motivation

Computational overhead underexplored in main paper: Footnote indicates 29% longer training (900k vs 700k steps for SiT), but detailed trade-off analysis relegated to appendix; wall-clock time on standard hardware not provided; GPU memory comparison limited

Hyperparameter generalization unclear: Multiple hyperparameters (α=0.05, γ=0.05) selected via ablation on ImageNet-LT with significant sensitivity (FID ranges 57.8-70.7 in Table 5); limited guidance for setting hyperparameters on new datasets; no cross-dataset validation

Mode collapse and failure cases incompletely analyzed: Figure 9 acknowledges method still fails for some tail classes (pretzel, orange); paper lacks systematic failure case analysis, performance across different imbalance factors, or discussion of extreme imbalance scenarios (>1000:1 ratios)

Incomplete comparative analysis: DiffROP comparison relegated to appendix; recent long-tail generation methods beyond CBDM/REPA not compared; UTLO GAN-based conditional-unconditional alignment only superficially discussed; concurrent work [41] using similar ideas not thoroughly compared

Evaluation limitations: FID_tail metric only examines bottom 30% of classes; no human perceptual evaluation; single imbalance factor tested; batch size sensitivity for contrastive learning not explored; head-tail trade-off analysis (Table 3) incomplete

Technical clarity issues: Notation inconsistencies (h_t^c, h_t^u subscripting); Eq. 5→7 transition relies on implicit Gaussian assumptions that should be stated upfront; Algorithm 1 formatting could be clearer; negative sample selection strategy in UCL underspecified

Experimental scope limitations: Only tested on image generation at ≤256×256 resolution; applicability to video, 3D, or other modalities unclear; architecture diversity limited to U-Net and DiT; scalability to higher resolutions (512×512+) not demonstrated

Limited practical guidance: CFG grid search (Appendix A.1) introduces confounding variables; hyperparameter selection process appears ad-hoc; 0.001 imbalance factor in Section A.3 unrealistic and poorly motivated; dataset-specific artifacts from [5] methodology not discussed
